story.title: Story 1: Attach Repositories to a Project or Process

result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 1 against the story AC/TCs and Flow 1 design, tracing the attach path from Fastify routes through source-management orchestration, Convex persistence/current-source mutation, and the project/process client surfaces. I also ran the mapped focused tests plus the story and epic gates.

newFindings.title: Project and process attach flows are still API-only because no UI action was implemented on either required surface
newFindings.evidence: The story scope explicitly includes a project-scoped attach UI action and a process-scoped attach UI action, and AC-1.1 expects the user to attach while viewing the project shell or process work surface (docs/spec-build/v2/epics/06--source-attachments-and-canonical-source-management/stories/01-attach-repositories-to-a-project-or-process.md:24-25,49-58). The project shell still renders only the existing Create process button plus passive sections (apps/platform/client/features/projects/project-shell-page.ts:71-99), the source attachment section is read-only markup with no form/button/callback (apps/platform/client/features/projects/source-attachment-section.ts:24-69), and the process work surface only renders existing controls/materials/history/side-work with no attach affordance or handler (apps/platform/client/features/processes/process-work-surface-page.ts:183-221). No client module calls the new POST /api/projects/:projectId/source-attachments or /api/projects/:projectId/processes/:processId/source-attachments routes, so a user cannot complete TC-1.1a or TC-1.1b from the required UI surfaces.

newFindings.title: Process-scoped attaches cannot show repository identity and scope on the process surface immediately after creation
newFindings.evidence: AC-1.2 requires the new attachment's repository identity and chosen scope to be visible immediately after creation (docs/spec-build/v2/epics/06--source-attachments-and-canonical-source-management/stories/01-attach-repositories-to-a-project-or-process.md:29-30,60-65). The process-surface contract cannot carry that data: ProcessSourceReference omits repositoryFullName and attachmentScope (apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts:318-330), the materials reader only projects displayName/purpose/accessMode/repositoryUrl/targetRef/hydrationState/updatedAt into currentSources (apps/platform/server/services/processes/readers/materials-section.reader.ts:90-99), and the process materials UI renders purpose/access/hydration/target ref/updated only (apps/platform/client/features/processes/process-materials-section.ts:220-253). The process attach API test likewise asserts only displayName and targetRef in materials.currentSources (tests/service/server/source-management-api.test.ts:223-234), while the lone TC-1.2 client test only covers the project shell source section (tests/service/client/source-attachment-section.test.ts:13-31).

productionPathFindings: Project and process surfaces ship without attach controls or route callers, so the attach workflow is API-only in the current runtime.
materials.currentSources omits repositoryFullName and attachmentScope, so a process-scoped attach cannot satisfy the required identity/scope visibility on the live process surface.
openQuestions: The story's Create Response table specifies a {"sourceAttachment": ...} wrapper, but Flow 1 and the implemented route schema return a bare SourceAttachmentSummary. Which response contract should downstream clients treat as canonical?
additionalObservations: The story gate (corepack pnpm run green-verify) and epic gate (corepack pnpm run verify-all) both passed, so the current automated suite is not exercising the missing UI attach path or the missing process-surface identity/scope fields.

The requested onboarding baseline path docs/onboarding/current-state-index.md was not present in this checkout, so repository orientation relied on the story/design/test-plan set plus code inspection.
